clue.text: Pay close attention to stuff in jotter

parts.note: to note something is to pay close attention to it
to pad is to stuff, as with a cushion

explanation.surface: Someone is told to concentrate on the stuff written in their notebook.
explanation.definitionFit: A jotter is a small book or block of paper for quick notes, which is what a notepad is.

clue.text: Number reduced, would you believe?

parts.note: less means reduced or diminished in amount

explanation.surface: Someone expresses surprise that a figure has come down.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole exclamatory phrase, and the question mark is part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: 'No less' is an exclamation stressing something surprising, as in 'the Queen, no less', much like 'would you believe it'.

clue.text: Street cop redeployed? That could be classified

indicators.note: a police officer redeployed is moved around, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A police officer moved to another beat might be a matter kept under wraps.
explanation.definitionFit: Classified documents are restricted to authorised people; the highest such grading is the hyphenated top-level secrecy term.

clue.text: Extremely severe correspondent, disregarding second page

indicators.note: disregarding means leaving out, so a letter is dropped from the correspondent

parts.note: a pen pal is a friend one corresponds with by letter
P is the abbreviation for page; here it is the second of the two in the word

explanation.surface: A letter writer becomes extremely harsh when ignoring the second page.
explanation.definitionFit: Penal measures or taxes are punitively harsh, so the word can mean extremely severe.

clue.text: Fish? Only after daughter left

indicators.note: after places the word for only behind the daughter-and-left pieces

parts.note: left over means remaining, so left gives over
sole means only, as in a sole survivor

explanation.surface: Someone eats fish only once their daughter has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a flatfish caught in the Channel and named after the English port of Dover.

clue.text: Artist's photographs must include American because of that

indicators.note: must include means the photographs word wraps round the American letter

parts.note: pics is informal for photographs
so means therefore, because of that

explanation.surface: A painter's photos have to feature something American for a reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artist's' reads as possessive but is 'Artist is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso was the Spanish painter who co-founded Cubism; the 's stands for 'is'.

clue.text: Guide, one in main story

indicators.note: in puts the numeral inside the story word

parts.note: the plot is the main storyline of a book or film
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A guide plays a part in the main story.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot guides ships into harbour, and to pilot is to steer or guide.

clue.text: G-man chose fancy dress

indicators.note: fancy here signals an elaborate rearrangement of the letters of G-man chose

explanation.surface: An FBI agent picks a costume for a fancy-dress party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy dress' reads as one phrase, but 'fancy' is the anagram signal and 'dress' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheongsam is a close-fitting Chinese dress with a high collar and a slit skirt.

clue.text: Colloquialisms in various languages

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits within the letters of various languages

explanation.surface: Informal expressions occur in many tongues.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is informal, colloquial vocabulary, a collective noun for such expressions.

clue.text: Connotation may be obvious, one added

indicators.note: added says the word for one is tacked on after the obvious word

parts.note: overt means open and obvious

explanation.surface: An implied meaning might become obvious if one more thing is added.
explanation.definitionFit: An overtone is a subtle extra implication of a word, the same idea as a connotation.

clue.text: Short row involving winning flower

indicators.note: involving means the shortened row word wraps round the winning word
short means the row word loses its last letter

parts.note: a line is a row, as of seats or people
up means ahead or winning, as in one up

explanation.surface: A short row of plants includes a prize-winning bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The lupin is a garden plant with tall spikes of pea-like blooms.

clue.text: Turning round, left a cove in resort

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort, sorting again, so the letters of left a cove are rearranged

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker turns back, having left a bay at a seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday place but is read as re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A volte-face is a complete reversal of opinion or policy, literally an about-turn.

clue.text: Suspect something's amiss, with master criminal holding everyone back

indicators.note: holding means the scrambled master letters wrap round the reversed everyone word
criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters of master are rearranged
back means the word for everyone is read backwards

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: Someone senses trouble when a criminal mastermind is holding everyone back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master criminal' reads as one phrase meaning a mastermind, but 'criminal' is the anagram signal working on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To smell a rat is the idiom for sensing that something is wrong or underhand.

clue.text: Near end of flight in darkness

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of flight

explanation.surface: A plane nears the end of its flight in the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the period of darkness between sunset and sunrise.

clue.text: Film noir: mafiosos and prince involved

indicators.note: involved means intricately tangled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dark thriller in which mobsters and a royal are mixed up.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is the kind of story film noir tells rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A killing driven by jealous rage or love is a staple plot of the moody crime films called film noir.

clue.text: Religious community, one briefly in control

indicators.note: in puts the shortened one inside the control word

parts.note: mastery means command or control

indicators.note: briefly means the word one is cut short by its last letter

explanation.surface: A religious order where a single person is in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A monastery is a house where a community of monks lives under religious vows.

clue.text: Snake tot's seen inside steam engine

indicators.note: seen inside means the adding word sits within the engine word

parts.note: puffer is a childish name for a steam train or engine
to tot up is to add; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A small child spots a snake inside an old steam train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a toddler but means add, as in totting up a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: The puff adder is a venomous African viper that inflates its body when threatened.

clue.text: Dicky, a guy far from relaxed

parts.note: dicky is British slang for unwell or shaky, as in a dicky heart
to guy someone is to mock or tease them

explanation.surface: A man called Dicky is described as tense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name; in British slang it means poorly or unreliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ill at ease means feeling uncomfortable or anxious, the opposite of relaxed.

clue.text: What's on top of cruise ship's comfy chair?

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: top of takes the first letter of cruise, as it is a down clue

parts.note: a liner is a large passenger ship; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A question about the best seat on board a cruise ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A recliner is an armchair whose back tilts back for lounging comfort.

clue.text: Tribe nervously feed lynx I tamed

indicators.note: nervously suggests jittery movement, so the letters of the fodder are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone anxiously feeds a wild cat they have tamed.
explanation.definitionFit: A family including grandparents, aunts, uncles and cousins is a clan, loosely a tribe.

clue.text: Bother about religious instruction? It's my job to!

definitions.text: Bother about religious instruction? It's my job to!

indicators.note: about means the nuisance word goes round the religious instruction letters

parts.note: a pest is a nuisance, something that bothers
RI is the abbreviation for religious instruction, a British school subject

explanation.surface: A cleric declares that worrying over religious teaching is their job.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and a definition spoken by the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman's role is to teach and care about matters of faith, as the speaker says.

clue.text: Spot insect shedding tail

indicators.note: shedding tail means the insect loses its final letter

parts.note: a locust is a swarming insect

explanation.surface: Someone spots an insect that is losing its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A locus is a place or position, which is what a spot means here.

clue.text: Song about a character lacking energy

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: lacking means the energy letter is dropped from the character word

parts.note: a role is a character in a play
E is the abbreviation for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A song about an actor's part that lacks spark.
explanation.definitionFit: A carol is a festive song, especially one sung at Christmas.

clue.text: Fierce debater's happy I returned list

parts.note: glad means happy

indicators.note: returned means the list word is read backwards

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties and who does them

explanation.surface: A combative speaker is pleased to get a list back.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively a gladiator is a person who fights hard in a public argument or cause.

clue.text: Superb piano

definitions.meaning: a large piano with horizontal strings

explanation.surface: Praise for a fine piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand means magnificent, and a grand is also the full-size concert piano.

clue.text: Home leased in cove

parts.note: in means at home
let means leased or rented out

explanation.surface: A house rented out on a small bay.
explanation.definitionFit: An inlet is a small arm of the sea reaching into the coast, much like a cove.

clue.text: Remind us, subtly, about a nanny

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the a
subtly suggests a cunning rearrangement of the letters of Remind us

explanation.surface: A gentle nudge to recall something about the nanny.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursemaid is a woman employed to look after children, the job of a nanny.

clue.text: Take off most of foliage

indicators.note: most of means the foliage word loses its last letter

parts.note: leaves make up the foliage of a plant

explanation.surface: An instruction to strip away most of a plant's greenery.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave is to depart, which is what take off means informally.

clue.text: Backing Ivy League university during revolutionary broadcast

indicators.note: during means the reversed name sits inside the revolutionary word

parts.note: a red is a revolutionary or communist

indicators.note: backing means the university's name is read backwards

parts.note: Yale is one of the US Ivy League universities

explanation.surface: Support for an elite American college aired during a revolutionary programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Relayed, as a past participle, means transmitted onward, as a signal is when broadcast.

clue.text: Withdraw in place of refuge

definitions.meaning: to withdraw, as an army does
a quiet, safe place to go

explanation.surface: Pull back into a safe haven.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means pulling back from danger; the noun is a secluded sanctuary one goes to.
